title: co-SNARK sidecar manifest
$comment: One schema for both paths (ARCHITECTURE.md section 7). `intake` selects the path: `direct` (the default) is the sidecar path; every other intake queues the request at the tip. The conditional at the end holds the path rules. The schema keeps the options REGISTER refuses until they are built (400): binding exact, state node under a queued intake, public_reads under intake direct, and chain-held state over the public-log bound (the apply log: the tag, one new commitment per output and 9 fields per element plus 15 per chain-held output, at most 4,094 fields, one public log: 453 elements in one output). The checks against the circuit's ABI, and the cross-field rules (every key loaded or stored is in range, every loaded client-held key is listed in consume, under a queued intake every loaded key has a commitment slot, a public read fills a public parameter filled by a request public name, the reserved operands only under a queued intake, the non-secret-shared intakes onchain and receipt taking no INPUT_SHARED source and none of the reserved shared values, a secret-shared intake taking at least one INPUT_SHARED app input or a shared $partial_note, each of INPUT_SHARED $blinding, $outcome_key and $outcome_tag (and under outcome partial $partial_note) and PUBLIC $inputs_hash exactly once in a private Field parameter and neither $user nor $user_nonce, under outcome partial no app input named recipient and under a non-secret-shared intake PUBLIC $partial_note exactly once with the round returning partial_note right after ok, the partial notes under no other outcome, a tree entry's store naming a key the round stores that no other entry declares, a round that loads and stores trees storing each tree it loads and creating none, with probe the header plus one slot per index input, under shared_onchain at most 9 clear inputs and shared values together (one request log)), are the machine's, at REGISTER.

circuit.$comment: 1 to 256 bytes of visible ASCII, as every name a binding hashes (REGISTER)

intake.$comment: direct: the client sends POST /v1/execute (the sidecar path); onchain: the request log carries the inputs in the clear (on-chain intake); receipt: three node receipts over the inputs (receipt intake); shared_receipt: three node receipts over the inputs commitment C, each node holding one Rep3 pair of every INPUT_SHARED value (secret-shared receipt intake); shared_onchain: the shares derived from the user's private request log, its hash stored beside the queue entry (secret-shared on-chain intake). ARCHITECTURE.md section 6, "Secret-shared intake"

state.$comment: a key loaded or stored and not listed is node; client needs intake direct, chain a queued intake

consume.$comment: intake direct only: a queued round's slot write is the spend

binding.$comment: queued intakes only; exact is deferred and refused at REGISTER

commitment_slot.$comment: queued intakes only: per loaded key, the public output carrying its old commitment; the new one is the key's outputs[].note_hash

^\\$state_keys\\.reads\\[.$comment: a tree the round loads: params, and store with new_hashes when the round stores it back; under access oblivious store without new_hashes (every such round stores the tree back and outputs no leaf hash)

^\\$state_keys\\.writes\\[.$comment: a tree the round creates: stored, not loaded; new_hashes under access clear, none under access oblivious

tree.$comment: queued intakes only: the layout of each tree-valued node-held key, declared once, under the key reference that loads it or, for a tree the round creates, the one that stores it; the reference a loaded tree is stored back at (store) takes this layout (ARCHITECTURE.md section 6, "Tree-valued keys")

outcome.$comment: queued intakes only: how the round's value reaches the user (ARCHITECTURE.md section 6, "Private outcomes"). partial (the default under every queued intake): the request commits a partial note, $partial_note, which the round completes inside the co-SNARK for a private result or the app's apply completes in public for a public one. none (onchain and receipt only, written out): the round completes no note and its public outputs go to the app's hook

public_read.$comment: A pinned public read and its freshness policy (ARCHITECTURE.md section 6, Pinned reads): exact (the default) requires the value the circuit used; epoch takes the value and its epoch from a call returning [value, epoch, previous] and accepts the current epoch or the one before; tolerance accepts a value within band of the current one. epoch_param only under epoch (required there), band only under tolerance (required there); the bounds of a band (an absolute below 2^128, relative_bps at most 10000) and the epoch read's parameters (each one public Field, the epoch right after the value) are the machine's checks.

contract.$comment: the called contract's address, or $self for the namespace's own contract (the machine substitutes the namespace; REGISTER refuses the namespace's address written out)

value.$comment: a request public name, $namespace, $state_keys.reads[i] / $state_keys.writes[j], a {const}, or under a queued intake a reserved operand $vk_hash, $user, $user_nonce, $new_leaf, $inputs_hash or $partial_note (one whole Field parameter each, never in a list, at most once; $new_leaf exactly when a tree has an open input; $user and $user_nonce under the non-secret-shared intakes only, $inputs_hash, a private parameter, under the secret-shared intakes only; $partial_note under the non-secret-shared intakes and outcome partial only, a clear app input the user supplies under the parameter's name, covered by inputs_hash; the others are not app inputs)

INPUT_SHARED.$comment: an app input's name, or under a secret-shared intake a reserved shared value: $blinding (the last element of C), $outcome_key, $outcome_tag, and under outcome partial $partial_note (the request's partial note); under shared_onchain each but $blinding is the user's, one correction in the request log; each fills one private Field

leaf_len.$comment: the elements of one leaf, its blinding included

probe.$comment: the most leaves a round touches: the header plus one per index input

header.$comment: leaf 0 is a fixed touch in slot 0

index.$comment: the app inputs naming position indices, in slot order

count.$comment: the app input saying how many index inputs the round uses (absent: all)

open.$comment: only with header true; access clear: the index input whose 0 opens a new leaf at $new_leaf; access oblivious: a PUBLIC 0/1 app input other than the index and count inputs, whose 1 opens $new_leaf in the first position slot

access.$comment: how the nodes reach the touched leaves: clear (the nodes see the indices and keep the tree of hashes in the clear) or oblivious (the index inputs are INPUT_SHARED, the leaves and hashes live in a distributed oblivious RAM and the paths reach the circuit as LOAD slices: ARCHITECTURE.md section 6, "The state-holder value"); one access per key across the namespace's rounds

keyed.$comment: access oblivious only: the tree is a sparse keyed map (ARCHITECTURE.md section 6, "The keyed map's manifest entry and REGISTER"): each index input is a key whose low depth bits are the leaf's path, the leaf's first element is the key, an empty leaf at the key's path proves its absence; depth 32 to 120 (MAX_MAP_DEPTH), leaf_len at least 3, no header, open, next_index or window

capacity.$comment: keyed only: log2 of the distinct DORAM addresses the map may ever hold (every address a round reads or writes; about 2 (depth - log2 keys) + leaf_len + 3 per key); default 18

params.$comment: under a loaded key reference only. access clear: leaves by LOAD of the key over probe * leaf_len (slice [0, probe * leaf_len]), the other three (indices required) private parameters by PUBLIC request names the scheduler fills from the nodes' trees. access oblivious: leaves, old_hashes and siblings the three LOAD slices of the key in that order ([0, probe * leaf_len], then probe, then probe * depth), no indices

next_index.$comment: access oblivious with open only: the public output of the header's append index after the round, from which the nodes keep their append index

width.$comment: the leaves the window holds: a power of two at most the network's bound (8, REGISTER) and at most 2^D

start.$comment: the app input naming the first leaf: read from leaf 0 when it is not below 2^D or not a multiple of width (the round flags it)

params.$comment: leaves by LOAD of the key after the slots (slice [probe * leaf_len, (probe + width) * leaf_len]), old_hashes (width) and siblings (the window root's D - log2 width) private parameters by PUBLIC request names the scheduler fills from the nodes' trees

window.$comment: under a loaded key reference only: a window of consecutive leaves the round reads after its slots and never writes (a window round, ARCHITECTURE.md section 6, "A read-only window on a tree key"); every LOAD of the key then has length (probe + width) * leaf_len

store.$comment: under a loaded key reference only: the reference the round stores the tree back at, a node-held key no other entry declares; its layout is this entry's

new_hashes.$comment: access clear, wherever the round stores the tree (with store, or under a stored key reference): the public output array of the new leaf hashes, one per slot; absent under access oblivious

tree.$comment: a tree that opens leaves (open) has a header (header true): the header leaf keeps the append index a new leaf's position is checked against (REGISTER refuses open without it)
